messages.text: Leicestershire's points deduction for poor pitch reduced

metadata.summary: Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19.
metadata.content: County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content County Championship: Leicestershire have eight points reinstated from 27-point deduction for poor pitch blamed on Bollywood film shoot Leicestershire chief executive Emma White confirms club will still appeal its deduction for the poor pitch that groundsman Callum Lewis later argued was due to a Bollywood film shoot; they will appeal against decision despite having eight points reinstated from original 27-point deduction Monday 28 September 2026 17:38, UK Image: Leicestershire were relegated following a defeat by champions Warwickshire in the last round of County Championship fixtures Leicestershire’s 27-point deduction for breaching pitch regulations in August's win over Glamorgan has been reduced to 19. The Foxes were relegated from Division One of the County Championship last week following an innings defeat by champions Warwickshire. Leicestershire's groundsman Callum Lewin had argued filming of an unscheduled Bollywood film - believed to be for a biopic of former India captain Sourav Ganguly - had taken place at the ground four days before the Glamorgan fixture between August 20-23, preventing the pitch from being covered for eight hours in bright sunshine and heatwave temperatures. messages.text: Does the Presidents Cup need changing to stop Team USA’s dominance?

metadata.summary: The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: Does Team USA's comeback win over Internationals show change is needed to make event more competitive? A different format? Fewer points on offer? LIV Golf players involved? Extra team events on the schedule? We look at possible ways to make the Presidents Cup even more competitive, following the United States' record-extending 11th consecutive win over the International Team Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Monday 28 September 2026 12:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final day of the Presidents Cup, where Team USA dominated the Sunday singles to close out a comeback victory over the International Team The United States maintained their Presidents Cup winning streak over the International Team, with the latest victory reigniting debate about whether change is needed in the biennial contest. Brandt Snedeker's side produced the largest final-day comeback in Presidents Cup history at Medinah, winning 9.5 of the 12 points on offer in the Sunday singles to close out a record-extending 11th consecutive victory. A 17-13 winning margin doesn't tell the full picture from a closer-than-expected contest, including a foursomes session sweep for the Internationals on Friday and them leading going into the final day for just the fourth time ever. messages.text: Man City CEO says fight against Premier League could take years to conclude

metadata.summary: Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told a meeting of fellow club chiefs their fight against the Premier League could take years to conclude, Sky News understands.
metadata.content: Man City CEO Ferran Soriano says fight against Premier League could take years to conclude amid reports of decision in 115 charges case | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City CEO Ferran Soriano says fight against Premier League could take years to conclude amid reports of decision in 115 charges case Reports on Friday claimed an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case – and that virtually all were found to have been proven; Man City deny all wrongdoing Rob Harris Sports correspondent, Sky News Monday 28 September 2026 20:38, UK Image: Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) alongside CEO Ferran Soriano (right) Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano has told a meeting of fellow club chiefs their fight against the Premier League could take years to conclude, Sky News understands. Soriano declined to answer questions from Sky News about the case as he left a private meeting of the executive board of the European Football Clubs' body in Copenhagen. But inside the room, sources have told Sky News that Soriano brought up the case against City, referencing the interest of other clubs - without directly mentioning the verdict of guilt over financial wrongdoing for years. McCarthy after losing Jaxson Dart for the rest of the 2026 NFL season. Dart suffered a year-ending knee injury early in New York's Week Two defeat to the Los Angeles Rams as they begin a new chapter in their first season under head coach John Harbaugh. Veteran Jameis Winston replaced Dart under center and started on Sunday as the Giants beat the Tennessee Titans to improve to 2-1 on the year. NFL Network reported that the Giants are trading a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Vikings in exchange for McCarthy, who was the 10th overall pick in the 2024 Draft.
